question: Who typically selects the individuals who serve as Village Health Workers?
explanation: Village Health Workers are chosen directly by their own community members to ensure trust and acceptance. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why are grassroots healthcare structures essential in rural Nigerian settings?

options.A: They bring basic care closer to populations far from formal health facilities
options.B: They completely replace the need for general hospitals and doctors
options.C: They focus solely on expensive surgical procedures and treatments
options.D: They operate independently without any community involvement

explanation: Local structures bridge geographical gaps, making health promotion accessible to remote populations. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is a core responsibility of a Community Health Committee?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations at the village square
options.B: Importing pharmaceutical drugs from foreign countries
options.C: Identifying local health needs through community dialogue
options.D: Issuing medical licenses to trained doctors

explanation: CHCs lead health planning by finding out what health problems affect their people most. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h2)

question: How do Community Health Committees help improve local health facilities?

options.A: By closing down clinics that do not meet international standards
options.B: By taking over the daily clinical duties of the resident midwives
options.C: By mobilizing community support for maintenance and resolving staff-patient grievances
options.D: By preventing community members from visiting formal hospitals

explanation: CHCs act as administrators and peacebuilders, keeping clinics functional and fostering good relationships. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main action a Village Health Worker should take when encountering a complicated medical case?

options.A: Keep the patient at home and administer strong prescription drugs
options.B: Promptly refer the patient to the nearest primary health center
options.C: Ignore the condition until it resolves on its own
options.D: Attempt to perform advanced surgery in the village

explanation: VHWs are trained to recognize danger signs and refer serious cases early to prevent complications. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h3)

question: A Village Health Worker visits a nursing mother and notices her baby has watery stools and signs of dehydration. What is the most appropriate initial step for the VHW?

options.A: Wait for three weeks to see if the diarrhea stops on its own
options.B: Tell the mother to stop feeding the baby all liquids immediately
options.C: Provide oral rehydration therapy and advise immediate referral if it worsens
options.D: Administer powerful intravenous antibiotics without a doctor's order

explanation: Managing simple childhood diarrhea with oral rehydration and knowing when to refer is a core VHW duty. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h3)

question: What primary barrier do VHWs and CHCs help overcome between rural dwellers and formal health staff?

options.A: The high cost of building multi-story teaching hospitals
options.B: A lack of international travel visas for nurses

explanation: Grassroots workers translate biomedical practices into terms the community understands and respect local traditions. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is increasing trust between rural communities and formal health systems important?

options.A: It removes the need for any government funding in the health sector
options.B: It ensures that traditional birth attendants are put out of business permanently
options.C: It encourages women to attend antenatal care and give birth in health facilities
options.D: It stops villagers from using herbal remedies for minor headaches

explanation: When communities trust the formal health system, more mothers seek professional care during pregnancy and delivery. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common local resource mobilization strategy for maternal emergencies?

options.A: Importing luxury ambulances from overseas donors
options.B: Community emergency transport schemes using local motorcycles or bicycles
options.C: Relying entirely on federal government helicopter drops
options.D: Building private airstrips in every rural village

explanation: Local transport schemes solve the delay in reaching health facilities during obstetric emergencies. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is relying on local resources better for health initiatives than depending solely on external donors?

options.A: Local resources promote long-term sustainability and true community ownership
options.B: Local materials are always more technologically advanced than foreign supplies
options.C: External donors always provide infinite funds that never run out
options.D: Communities refuse to use any service that receives foreign assistance

explanation: Programs backed by local contributions survive even when external grants or donor projects end. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by community-led health initiatives?

options.A: Poor integration between formal health boards and grassroots groups
options.B: Volunteer burnout due to a lack of regular financial compensation
options.C: Guaranteed lifetime salaries and pensions for all Village Health Workers
options.D: Political interference from local elites in committee leadership

explanation: VHWs generally work on a voluntary basis without guaranteed salaries or pensions, which is a major challenge. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h6)

question: What measure helps maintain the motivation of Village Health Workers over the long term?

options.A: Increasing their workload without any communication or feedback
options.B: Removing all contact between them and formal medical doctors
options.C: Replacing them with new volunteers every single month
options.D: Providing regular supportive supervision, refresher training, and recognition

explanation: Consistent support, updated knowledge, and appreciation keep volunteer health workers engaged and motivated. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h6)
